transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess my manager at the restaurant wanted me to come in. I really think I'm doing mostly okay, but... well, there was a little bit of a mix-up at work recently. It's actually really embarrassing to talk about, but I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. 

I guess I sort of scared everyone during my shift. I started, um, kind of freezing up in the middle of service. Or just doing things a little out of order? Like... they found me standing over by the soda station, and I was just holding the cash drawer key, repeating table numbers to myself instead of actually closing out the checks. I really didn't mean to cause any trouble for anyone, I promise. Does that make sense, why they'd want me to come see you?
When you were repeating those numbers to yourself, did it feel like you were hearing someone else's voice, or was it just your own thoughts?

Um, well... I guess it's a little bit of both? I mean, mostly it's just my own thoughts, like anyone else trying to remember things when it's busy. But... sometimes, and I really hope this doesn't sound too crazy, but sometimes when I'm closing up at work, or even just at home in my own kitchen, I... I hear a woman's voice. 

She'll just say my name, or tell me I'm doing the count wrong. It's so clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize that... well, that nobody else is there, and nobody else heard it. I feel so silly when it happens. Is that... is that normal when you're just really stressed out? I'm trying really hard not to let it affect my work, I promise.
How long have you been hearing this woman's voice, and does it happen every day?

Um... I guess it's been... maybe about four months? That the voice has been really clear like that, anyway. I try really hard to push it away, so it doesn't happen every single day, I promise. I really am trying my best to just focus on my work. 

And... well, there's something else, but I feel really bad even saying it out loud because I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my job or being a bad team player. But around that same time, about four months ago... I started getting this really strong feeling—like, a really firm belief—that some of my coworkers, and even some of the customers, were... well, targeting me. Like they were doing things on purpose to mess me up or get me in trouble. 

I know it's awful to think that about people, and I try so hard to just smile and be polite to everyone anyway. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this? I'm so sorry if it makes me sound awful, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right and giving you what you need.

Over the past four months, have you noticed any significant periods where your mood felt extremely low, or alternatively, periods where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or like you didn't need much sleep?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I get a little bummed out sometimes if I feel like I'm not doing a good job at work, but not... not extremely low or anything like that. I really try my best to keep a positive attitude and a smile on my face for the customers, no matter what. 

And I definitely need my rest. I try to make sure I get enough sleep every night so I can be ready for my shifts, so I haven't had any times where I'm just bouncing off the walls or talking a million miles an hour without sleeping. I just try to be as steady and reliable as I can be. I hope that's a good thing? Did I answer that right, or did you mean something else?
Outside of those moments at work, have you ever felt like your thoughts get jumbled, or that you have trouble keeping your sentences organized and on track?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I have that problem. I mean, I guess everyone loses their train of thought for a quick second if they're distracted, right? But... no, I feel like I'm pretty good at keeping my sentences together. 

I really pride myself on being a good communicator, especially since I have to talk to my tables all day. I always try my hardest to make sure I'm speaking clearly and being polite, so I haven't noticed my words getting all mixed up or anything like that. I really try to stay organized. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining things clearly for you today, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you found it difficult lately to feel motivated to do things you used to enjoy, or do you feel like you have less interest in spending time with your friends or family?

Um... well... I guess I have been a little less active lately. I don't want to sound lazy or anything, I promise I'm not! I still go to work and do my best there. But... yeah, I guess I haven't been doing some of the things I used to do as much. 

Like, I used to love going for walks on the beach, and baking, and gardening, and... oh, writing in my journal. But lately, I just... I don't really do those things much anymore. And I feel terrible about this, but when my husband tries to talk with me, I... I mostly just sit there. It's not that I don't love him, I really do! It's just... it feels like I can't get myself to care or, like, start anything. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds awful, like I'm being a bad wife or just giving up. I really don't mean to be like that. I just feel so drained sometimes. Is that... is that normal? I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying all this, I just want to be honest so you can help me.
When you feel that your coworkers are targeting you, do you have a specific idea of why they would be doing this, or how they are going about it?

Um... well... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my coworkers, because I know everyone works really hard and the restaurant business is stressful. But... I just keep feeling like a couple of the other servers, and even one of our regular customers, are... well, they're watching me. 

Like, they watch really closely how I ring things into the POS system. And I keep finding these little signs on the tickets... like they're leaving clues to prove they're trying to get me fired. I know that sounds a little crazy, and I'm really sorry to even say it. My husband tells me I'm overthinking it and that it's just normal restaurant mess-ups or typos on the tickets. And I really try to believe him, I do! I just want to do a good job and not cause any trouble for the managers. 

I really don't want you to think I'm paranoid or a bad team player. I try so hard to get along with everyone. Does that make sense? Or am I just making a big deal out of nothing? I really value your opinion on this.
Outside of feeling drained, have you noticed that your facial expressions have become less expressive, or that your speech has become more monotone or limited in range?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really hope not! I know how important it is to be friendly and smile, especially at work. I always try my best to greet my tables with a big smile and sound cheerful, because I want them to have a good experience. 

My husband hasn't said anything about me looking... blank or sounding flat, either. I think I still talk the same way I always have. I really try to make sure I'm showing people that I'm listening and that I care about what they're saying. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was ignoring them or being rude. 

Do I look okay right now? I hope I don't seem like I'm not expressing myself well to you. I'm really trying to communicate clearly.
